questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose this destination since I originally had a stay planned in Jerusalem which I had to cancel after the terror attack in October 2023 - I chose Norway/Oslo since I considered it to be a very safe country where I did not think that there would be any unforeseen safety issues. Further, I have not been to Norway before and I thought that it would be interesting to experience living in another Scandinavian country. I also like outdoor activities a lot, and Norway is a great place to do hiking and tenting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had some difficulties with the registration for courses since the person who was in charge of helping me with which courses I could take were not very quick at replying my emails and often forgot them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had not received any information about the introduction week before I arrived and they did not reply to my emails, so i had to go to the counseling office, but they were very helpful, when I got there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. They have a housing organisation called SIO and i think that all exchange students who applied through this organisation got some housing. And is was quite cheap compared to prices in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Even though some of the housing seems like it's a bit far from centrum of Oslo it's fine living there since it's easy and affordable to get around with the metro.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a internetpage where all the registration takes place. But I could not do the registration myself but had to wait for a person from the student counseling to allow me to register to the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a person from the student counselling who helped me with the registration. I emailed with her before my stay.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up registering for the classes a bit late since it was difficult to find classes that I could take, so there was some classes i wanted to do but that i could not register for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You should know that at the University of Oslo it is possible to register for classes after the semester has started. I was very confused about that, since you have to register quite early at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses where at Master level. I had both courses at the faculty of health and sociology and i think that the courses at sociology was much more difficult than at the faculty of health. Otherwise i think that the courses were easier than at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty much the same. We both had lectures and seminars (group-work) which is also the case at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
User and Family Involvement
Politics of Sustainability in Public Health - Data-Driven Critical Conceptual Analysis
Complex Interventions and Implementation
Public Health and Non-communicable Diseases
Population Health and Health Inequalities

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend "Politics of Sustainability in Public Health - Data-Driven Critical Conceptual Analysis", since i think this was a course that were most different from the courses i can take at UCPH and it was also quite interesting.

questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, transportation and housing were less expensive than expected. There was nothing, that were more.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN had a lot of activities e.g. hiking and dinners together with other exchange students. The university also had a lot of different student organisations with different activities like dancing, outdoor and music.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend participating in the ESN activities. Most of them are free, and it's an easy way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking some trips to other cities in Norway to experience the nature there. I think Trondheim was particularly beautiful to visit and you can go cross country-skiing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy since the Norwegian culture is not very different from the Danish, and it is even possible to just speak Danish with the Norwegian people..

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was no cultural differences that were challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It seemed like the Norwegian people are very fond of outdoor activities and there are lot of different possibilities which i enjoyred a lot. it is for instance possible to rent or borrow outdoor gear in most fitness centers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Engage in some of the ESN activities to meet other exchange students. 
2. Go on some hikes to experience the Norwegian nature. 
3. I did some courses in Norwegian and it was quite easy to follow the lectures and i would recommend doing that if you want to meet Norwegian students. You are allowed to do exams in Danish.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience living in another Scandinavian country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was the registration process, since i felt it was quite stressful that i did not know which courses i could take before going to Norway.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
